column1: # agent-comms reviewer model/effort policy map — THE one place a vendor model id is named.
# Read only by helpers/acp.sh (`resolve`, and every policy accessor), from the file installed
# beside it. There is deliberately no environment override for the map itself: operator
# intent enters as the COMMS_ACP_CODEX_MODEL / COMMS_ACP_CODEX_EFFORT pins, never as a
# second table. Every value here reaches a TOML file that governs a reviewer's sandbox, so
# acp.sh allowlists each one on read and refuses the whole map if any row is malformed.
# A model update is ONE edit here plus `version`, never a change to the classifier rubric.
# Bump `version` on every change: it is recorded with every resolved turn (policy.tsv,
# turn.tsv), so a row can always be joined to the table that produced it.
# Rows (TAB-separated; `#` starts a comment line):
#   version     <id>
#   capability  <provider> <transport> <eligible|fixed|unsupported> <application mechanism>
#               <evidence source> <versions tested> <notes>
#   baseline    <provider> <transport> <model> <effort>
#   tier        <provider> <transport> <fast|balanced|strong> <model>[,<fallback model>...]
#               an ORDERED preference: the first model the reviewer runtime can serve
#   effort      <provider> <transport> <low|medium|high|xhigh> <provider-effort>
#   pair        <provider> <transport> <model> <comma-separated efforts the model accepts>
#               [<minimum codex runtime version that can serve it>]
#   ceiling     <provider> <transport> <model> <effort>   the operator's "use max" pair
#               (COMMS_REVIEW_MAX=1): the strongest model at its highest accepted effort
#   disabled    <provider> <transport> <model> <reason>   a model the provider has announced but nothing
#               can serve yet. Its tier/pair rows may already be written; resolve REFUSES it (a pin) and
#               a routed tier skips it, so deleting this one row is the whole act of enabling it.
#   limit       <provider> <transport> <model> <limit_id>   a model the provider meters under a
#               usage limit of its OWN (codex's Spark models, for example), named by the limit_id
#               its rate-limit records report. A model with no row spends the provider's shared
#               limit. Read only to REPORT a leg's spend (policy record `limit_id`, `review-route
#               plan`, result.json "route"); it never changes which model or effort runs.
# Transports: acp-mounted = a mounted review turn with an isolated provider home (the only
# place a policy is both APPLIED and ATTESTED); acp = an unmounted ACP turn (the operator's own
# provider config runs); headless = the detached, parent-brokered CLI runner (grok: nothing applied; gemini via agy:
# applied and attested).
# Capability `eligible` means a routed decision may change the concrete pair. `fixed` means the
# baseline (plus pins) is applied and attested but routing is ignored. `unsupported` means nothing
# is applied, so nothing may be claimed. Only a provider/transport whose controls AND per-turn
# evidence were established is eligible; a control that merely exists in an adapter is recorded
# in the mechanism text, not enabled.
# Evidence (2026-09-22, local and read-only): codex models_cache.json (codex-cli 0.155.1 and the
# isolated home's 0.154.0), @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 1.12.0 dist, acpx 0.13.1 dist,
# @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp 0.60.0 dist, grok 1.0.40 --help + models_cache.json.
# Tier labels follow the provider's own model descriptions: luna "fast and affordable", terra
# "balanced", astra "most capable".
# LIVE PROBES, 2026-09-22 (acpx 0.13.1, codex-acp 1.12.0 bundling codex 0.154.0, ChatGPT auth):
# - gpt-6-sol / gpt-6-luna (released 2026-09-22): the adapter's BUNDLED codex 0.154.0 is refused
#   gpt-6-luna for a ChatGPT-auth account (400; no model metadata, so no effort option) and does
#   not advertise gpt-6-sol. With CODEX_PATH at the installed codex 0.155.1 both answered and were
#   attested (gpt-6-luna/low, gpt-6-sol/medium). Hence the 0.155.0 minimum on their pair rows and
#   the gpt-5.6 fallbacks in each tier.
# - The rollout records the requested model/effort even when the API call then fails, so a
#   turn_context alone does not prove the turn succeeded; the canary and reply-check gates stay.
# - A resumed codex session adopted a changed config.toml (one observation); `acpx set` of
#   model/reasoning_effort is honoured BEFORE the first prompt and fails ("Internal error") after
#   one. Sessions are still keyed by policy digest, so no correctness rests on either.
# GPT-6.1-SOL, 2026-09-29 (codex-acp 1.12.0 bundling codex 0.154.0; installed codex 0.159.0;
# ChatGPT auth). Made the codex baseline and the first preference of `balanced` at the operator's
# request on release day. OPERATOR DECISION (map 2026-09-29.2): gpt-6.1-sol is the DEFAULT, not the
# strongest. OpenAI describes it as the everyday workhorse and gpt-6-astra as the frontier model, so
# `strong` and the `use max` ceiling stay gpt-6-astra; 6.1-sol leads the baseline and `balanced` only.
# (Map 2026-09-29.1 had also put 6.1-sol first in `strong` and at the ceiling, which collapsed the
# baseline, `strong` and `use max` onto one model; the verifier flagged it and .2 reverts that.)
# - Catalog, per client (`<codex> debug models` for each installed release under
#   ~/.codex/packages/standalone/releases/, and the adapter's bundled binary): only 0.159.0 lists
#   gpt-6.1-sol ("Latest workhorse model for coding and everyday work", efforts
#   low,medium,high,xhigh,max,ultra, default low). 0.155.1 through 0.158.0 list gpt-6-astra,
#   gpt-6-sol and gpt-6-luna and nothing newer; the bundled 0.154.0 lists gpt-6-astra alone.
#   No gpt-6.1 luna or astra is listed, so `fast` is unchanged.
# - Live (`printf 'Reply with exactly the word PONG…' | CODEX_HOME=<isolated home, copied
#   auth.json> <codex> exec --skip-git-repo-check -s read-only -m gpt-6.1-sol
#   -c model_reasoning_effort=low --json -`): 0.159.0 answered PONG; 0.158.0 and the bundled 0.154.0
#   were refused (400 "The 'gpt-6.1-sol' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT
#   account", after "Model metadata for `gpt-6.1-sol` not found"). Hence the 0.159.0 minimum on its
#   pair row: the adapter's bundled codex cannot serve it, so a mounted turn needs CODEX_PATH at an
#   installed codex >= 0.159.0 (acp.sh auto-detects it on PATH). On an older runtime the baseline
#   is REFUSED (it has no fallback; `acp.sh doctor` and `comms.sh setup` say so), and a routed
#   `balanced` tier falls to its next model. The ceiling (gpt-6-astra) needs no minimum.
# - Mounted (`runphase.sh run --agent codex --via acp --no-deliver` from a worktree carrying this
#   map, COMMS_ACP_CODEX_PATH unset so the installed 0.159.0 was auto-detected; map 2026-09-29.1,
#   whose baseline row .2 keeps): the canary passed and the turn completed; turn.tsv requested
#   gpt-6.1-sol/xhigh, adapter_check match (acpx config_options), observed_model/effort
#   gpt-6.1-sol/xhigh from the isolated rollout, session_created_runtime 0.159.0.
# GEMINI, 2026-10-07 — the Antigravity CLI (`agy`, 1.3.1), run DIRECTLY (no ACP). Exercised live against the
# operator's own login; the Gemini CLI this provider used to launch (`gemini --acp`) was retired for
# individual accounts on 2026-06-18, and its rows, isolated-home arm and chat-record reader are gone.
# - Transport: `headless` (agy is a detached, parent-brokered CLI turn, like grok). There is no mounted/unmounted
#   split: agy has no isolated home to apply a policy to, so the policy is a launch argument and the same
#   `headless` row governs a review and a consult.
# - Application: `--model <model>-<effort>`. agy lists every variant as its own id (`agy models`:
#   gemini-3.1-pro-high, gemini-3.1-pro-low, gemini-3.8-flash-low|medium|high, ...). `--model <model> --effort
#   <effort>` is the same pair, but agy's init event then echoes only the bare model; the combined id is echoed
#   whole, so ONE per-turn record evidences model AND effort. agy itself refuses a pair it does not know
#   (`--model gemini-3.1-pro --effort xhigh`: "no xhigh effort (available: low, high)"), before any turn.
# - Evidence: the `init` event of the turn's own stream-json output (helpers/agy_stream.py `attest`). The
#   canary and the review prompt each carry one; the review's is what gates publication.
# - Hence capability `eligible`: control (the combined id) AND per-turn evidence (the echoed id) exist.
# - Efforts: gemini-3.1-pro has low and high; gemini-3.8-flash has low, medium and high. `xhigh` has no row: a
#   routed candidate of it falls back to the baseline, recorded.
# - Ranking: Artificial Analysis (API, read 2026-10-07) puts Gemini 3.8 Flash (High) above Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview
#   on both indices (Intelligence 40.9 vs 29.7, Coding 76.3 vs 68.8), and there is no 3.8 Pro as of 2026-10. So
#   gemini-3.8-flash at `high` is the baseline and ceiling, and gemini-3.1-pro stays only as the fallback row.
# - Tiers: one model leads all three; a routed candidate's own effort separates them (fast = low, balanced =
#   medium, strong = high). gemini-3.1-pro trails `strong` and is what a pin selects for an account the 3.8 model
#   is not served to.
# - gemini-3.8-flash is not served to every account (SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED, google-antigravity/antigravity-cli
#   issue 1180). That is an account fact, not a map fact: the turn is recorded `model-unavailable`.
# - agy has no rate-limit record on disk: a refusal is classified from its own diagnostics (`rate-limited`).
version
# No mapped model has a usage limit of its own yet, so there are no `limit` rows: every mapped codex
# model spends the shared codex limit. A row is added with the evidence that the model is served
# AND of the limit_id its rollouts report — never from a model's name alone.
capability

# everyday value (gpt-6.1-sol the latest workhorse, so `balanced` and the baseline), luna
# narrow/easily checked work. No model is in two tiers, so a baseline gpt-6.1-sol turn records
